title: Unattributed prefetch tokens from KV-cache pruning leading to billing deltas
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Several customers reported unexplained billing deltas over the last 36 hours: usage ledger shows unbilled token consumption during rolling cache pruning events. Problem appears in both Hosted and Dedicated deployments and correlates with autoscaler-driven node evacuation (k8s node drain) that triggers KV-cache pruning and prefetch eviction.

Observed impact:
- Customers A and D saw 0.5%–2% token delta on daily invoices (investigated via customer support tickets and sample ledgers).
- Ledger attribution: requests were visible in serving logs but missing a matching metering record or attributed to internal system tenant.
- A subset of streaming sessions resumed after failover and generated additional prefetch requests that were double-counted in temporary caches but never reconciled in the metering ingest pipeline.

Investigation notes & hypothesis (timeline):
- 2026-03-01 03:20 UTC: First anomalous customer report from Support (ticket #SUP-9228).
- 2026-03-01 04:00 UTC: Correlation with node drain in us-west-2 dedicated pool (deployments team).
- 2026-03-01 08:30 UTC: Reproduced locally by forcing KV-cache prune during active prefix prefetch; observed prefetch request IDs emitted without tenant header in a narrow race window.
- Hypothesis: a race between cache eviction and request attribute propagation causes prefetch rays to get emitted to internal prefetch queue with tenant ID lost, so metering ingest assigns them to a fallback internal tenant and later ledger backfill merges lead to missing attribution or duplicate accounting when failover replay occurs.

Root cause (current working theory):
- KV-cache pruning path uses an async background task that republishes prefetch RPCs to a warm-up queue. During node evacuation the tenant-context propagation can be dropped for prefetch retries if the request context has been canceled and not rehydrated before re-enqueue. This yielded two distinct failures: (1) some tokens were emitted without tenant metadata (so they were either unbilled or billed to an internal tenant), and (2) some prefetches retried after failover were reprocessed by both the streaming path and the backfill path leading to half- or double-counted tokens depending on ingest timing.

Proposed fix: engineering plan
- Short-term mitigation (hotfix): when re-enqueueing prefetch tasks, attach a mandatory immutable metadata blob with tenant_id and request_id before any async cancellation points; if not present, drop and increment a telemetry counter. Deploy as a canary to hosting-edge and a subset of dedicated pools. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6478)
- Medium-term (robustness): move prefetch warm-up to synchronous transactional enqueue that requires tenant attribution; add end-to-end idempotency keys for prefetch tokens processed by metering ingest.
- Metering pipeline change: add a reconciliation job that detects untagged internal-tenant tokens and attempts to join them with candidate requests using (approx) request_id, timestamp, and node_id heuristics. Run nightly and surface candidate matches to finance for manual reconciliation until automatic rule has high precision.

Test plan:
- Unit tests covering context propagation on prune and re-enqueue paths.
- Integration test that simulates node drain and confirms no prefetch emitted with empty tenant header.
- End-to-end metering integration test asserting idempotency for prefetch token ingestion.
- Canary rollout to 10% traffic on hosted API and a single dedicated cluster; monitor metering diffs and error counters for 48 hours.

Deployment & rollback plan:
- Merge PR and cut canary build (runtime-1.22-canary.3). Roll to hosted-edge canary first.
- Monitor dashboards: metric.metering.unattributed_prefetch_count, metric.metering.duplicate_token_alerts, cost-ledger-delta.% (links below).
- If unattributed_prefetch_count decreases to baseline and duplicate_token_alerts fall to zero for 24 hours, proceed to 50% and then full rollout.
- Rollback: revert canary build and redeploy prior image; unblock by toggling feature flag prefetch_strict_attr=off.

Monitoring & success criteria:
- < 5 unattributed prefetch events per region per hour within 72 hours of full rollout.
- Customer ledger delta for previously affected customers reduced to within normal variance (<=0.1%) for the next billing cycle.

Follow-ups & open questions:
- Confirm whether private/on-prem packages have equivalent prefetch paths and will need patching (likely yes).
- Determine if quota or rate-limiters should be exempt from rehydrate-on-evict to avoid denial during drain.
- Finance reconciliation: schedule a manual backfill window for affected accounts if automatic reconciliation precision < 95%.

References and artifacts:
- Support tickets: SUP-9228, SUP-9241, SUP-9250
- Repro PR and test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6478
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KV-Cache+Prefetch+Metering+Incidents
- Kibana dashboard: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/dashboards#/view/abcd-usage-deltas
